The forecasts of inflation in the euro area for the years 2006-2007 have remained unchanged, while inflation forecasts in the United States for the same period have been slightly revised downwards.
October marked a slight decline in the annual growth of consumer prices in the euro area to 1.6% as compared with 1.7% in September.
The annual rate of growth in the United States also decreased (to 1.3% from 2.1% y/y in September).
The decline of inflation in the euro area and the United States has been largely driven by a decrease in crude oil prices.

Since the second half of 2005, a high growth rate of consumer loans to households has been sustained and in October 2006 it amounted to 20.0% y/y.
Also housing loans has been growing fast; in October 2006 their rate of growth reached 52.3%.
